notes: BC Assessment is a province-wide Crown corporation under the Assessment Act that produces a uniform annual assessment roll for all properties (market value as of 1 July); this is structurally different from Alberta's municipal-level assessment + provincial equalized-assessment model and is described accurately rather than forced into the Alberta shape. No provincial 'equalized assessment' report exists. Municipalities receive the assessment roll (via Data Advice and Year-End Assessment Roll Report) and independently set tax rates on those values; the Community Charter defines 'assessed value' as value determined under the Assessment Act. Vancouver publishes an Annual Financial Report (audited consolidated statements under PSAB), annual Budget / Five-Year Financial Plan, and annual Tax Rating Bylaws (plus land-assessment averaging bylaws); no document titled 'Financial Information Return' or exact Alberta FIR equivalent was found. Victoria publishes a multi-year Financial Plan, Annual Report containing audited financial statements, and Statement of Financial Information under the Financial Information Act. BC Housing Rental Assistance Program (RAP) and Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters (SAFER) use an internal income/rent-gap formula with province-wide maximum rent ceilings; primary framework documents do not name CMHC's Rental Market Survey as an input to rate-setting (unlike the Ontario/NS portable benefits already in the corpus). Canada-BC Housing Benefit exists but is registry-selected rather than formula-driven against RMS. Primary documents found for BC Assessment (Assessment Act, roll quality metrics referencing IAAO, annual service-plan reports, Data Advice, Year-End Assessment Roll Report), BC Budget and Fiscal Plan, Vancouver budget/financial reports/tax-rating bylaws, Victoria financial plan/annual report/SOFI, and BC Housing RAP framework. Searching beyond these did not surface additional verifiable primary-report nodes or evidenced edges of equal strength.

proposed_reports.title: BC Assessment Authority (property assessment roll and related products)
proposed_reports.description: Provincial Crown corporation established under the Assessment Authority Act and Assessment Act that produces the annual uniform province-wide assessment roll for more than two million properties, valuing most at market value as of 1 July of the preceding year; supplies the completed, revised and supplementary rolls (and Data Advice extracts) to municipalities, regional districts and provincial taxing authorities as the sole base for property-value taxation.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: annual (roll completed by 31 December; notices mailed early January; revised roll after Property Assessment Review Panel; weekly/monthly Data Advice updates)

proposed_reports.title: Assessment Roll Quality (Assessment-to-Sales Ratio and Coefficient of Dispersion metrics)
proposed_reports.description: Annual public reporting of median Assessment-to-Sales Ratio (ASR) and Coefficient of Dispersion (COD) for residential, strata-residential and non-residential properties against International Association of Assessing Officers (IAAO) standards, demonstrating accuracy and uniformity of the assessment roll.

proposed_reports.title: Year-End Assessment Roll Report
proposed_reports.description: Report supplied to taxing authorities covering assessment trends, risk-to-roll, roll stability, market-movement summaries (July 1 values), assessment initiatives, information-exchange requirements and legislative/case-law updates to support municipal financial planning and appeal-reserve allocation.

proposed_reports.title: BC Assessment Annual Service Plan Report
proposed_reports.description: Statutory annual report under the Budget Transparency and Accountability Act comparing actual results against the three-year service plan, including assessment-roll quality metrics, financial statements and performance against mandate to produce uniform assessments.

proposed_reports.title: Budget and Fiscal Plan (British Columbia)
proposed_reports.description: Principal annual budget document presenting the three-year fiscal plan (revenues, expenses, capital, debt), economic review and outlook, major assumptions and risks, tax measures and federal-transfer projections; tabled with the Estimates and accompanying ministry/Crown service plans.

proposed_reports.title: City of Vancouver Annual Financial Report
proposed_reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements and accompanying management discussion prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards, reporting financial position, results of operations, cash flows and accumulated surplus for the City of Vancouver.

proposed_reports.title: City of Vancouver Operating and Capital Budget / Five-Year Financial Plan
proposed_reports.description: Annual operating budget and multi-year capital plan setting expenditure authorities, property-tax levy, utility rates and service levels; approved by Council and used as the baseline for subsequent quarterly reviews and the following year's tax-rating bylaws.

proposed_reports.title: City of Vancouver Tax Rating Bylaws (General Purpose Tax and related)
proposed_reports.description: Annual bylaws establishing municipal general-purpose tax rates (and rates for Metro Vancouver Regional District, Municipal Finance Authority and other authorities after land-assessment averaging) applied to the BC Assessment taxable values for each property class; enacted after budget approval and before the statutory May deadline.

proposed_reports.title: City of Victoria Financial Plan (multi-year)
proposed_reports.description: Five-year financial plan adopted by Council under the Community Charter, setting operating and capital expenditures, property-tax revenue requirements and tax-distribution policy for the City of Victoria.

proposed_reports.title: City of Victoria Annual Report (audited financial statements) and Statement of Financial Information
proposed_reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements prepared under Public Sector Accounting Standards together with the Statement of Financial Information required by the Financial Information Act, reporting revenues (including taxation), expenses, financial position and accumulated surplus.

proposed_reports.title: BC Housing Rental Assistance Program (RAP) and related frameworks
proposed_reports.description: Provincial portable rental-assistance program providing monthly benefits to eligible low-income families (and parallel SAFER for seniors) calculated from an income/rent-gap formula subject to province-wide maximum rent ceilings; administered by BC Housing under published program frameworks.
proposed_reports.publication_cadence: ongoing (framework updated periodically; benefit parameters reviewed annually)

dependencies.basis: BC Assessment's own financial statements and Annual Service Plan Report are prepared in accordance with Public Sector Accounting Standards established by the Public Sector Accounting Board.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The accompanying financial statements of the British Columbia Assessment Authority (the “Authority”) are the responsibility of the Authority’s management and have been prepared in compliance with legislation and in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles for public sector organizations established by the Public Sector Accounting Board of the Chartered Professional Accountants.

dependencies.basis: The ASR and COD metrics are calculated directly from the assessment roll values produced by BC Assessment and the corresponding sale prices of properties that sold near the July 1 valuation date.
dependencies.evidence_quote: An Assessment to Sales Ratio (ASR) is calculated by dividing the property’s assessed value by the property’s selling price. ... For the 2026 Assessment Roll, BC Assessment’s median ASR for single-family residential properties, strata residential properties ... and non-residential are within the targeted range.

dependencies.basis: Municipal tax rates are applied to the taxable assessed values supplied by BC Assessment; the Community Charter defines assessed value as the value determined under the Assessment Act, and Vancouver's rating bylaws and tax notices explicitly use the BC Assessment roll as the tax base.
dependencies.evidence_quote: "assessed value" means assessed value determined under the Assessment Act; "assessment roll" means an assessment roll within the meaning of the Assessment Act

dependencies.basis: The annual tax-rating bylaws are enacted after Council approval of the operating budget and set the rates required to raise the property-tax levy authorized in that budget (subject to land-assessment averaging).
dependencies.evidence_quote: On November 25, 2025, Council approved the 2026 Operating Budget based on a Council-directed property tax increase of 0%. ... 2026 Rating By-law – General Purpose Tax ... that establishes the 2026 municipal general purpose tax rates

dependencies.basis: The City's consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public-sector accounting standards.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The financial statements are the responsibility of the City of Vancouver’s management and have been prepared in compliance with Section 167 of the Community Charter and in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles approved by the Public Sector Accounting Board.

dependencies.basis: The City of Victoria's audited consolidated financial statements are prepared in compliance with the Community Charter and Public Sector Accounting Board standards.
dependencies.evidence_quote: The financial statements are the responsibility of the City of Victoria’s management and have been prepared in compliance with Section 167 of the Community Charter and in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles approved by the Public Sector Accounting Board.

dependencies.basis: Property-tax revenue requirements in the Financial Plan are calculated from the taxable assessed values supplied by BC Assessment; tax rates are set on that base after the plan is adopted.
dependencies.evidence_quote: In 2026, the increase in revenue needed from property taxes is $14.185 million over 2025, resulting in an overall tax increase of 7.28 per cent ... This will result in an average property tax increase of $323 for an average residential property assessed at $1,015,000

dependencies.basis: The fiscal plan's revenue forecast explicitly incorporates the Canada Health Transfer (and related health agreements) as a major federal contribution, with growth assumptions tied to national nominal GDP.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Federal transfers include $2.2 billion over three years in targeted federal funding for health services (e.g., $447 million under Aging with Dignity agreement, $653 million for expanded public coverage for diabetes and hormone replacement therapy, $1.1 billion for extension of Working Together to Improve Health Care for Canadians agreement, in addition to Canada Health Transfer).

dependencies.basis: Canada Health and Social Transfers are forecast as a combined line item whose growth is based on national nominal GDP; the plan treats them as material federal contributions to provincial revenue.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Canada Health Transfer and Canada Social Transfer (increasing 4.4% annually, based on national nominal GDP forecasts).

dependencies.basis: The economic outlook and revenue forecasts rely on Statistics Canada national-accounts and related series (GDP, labour-force, CPI, housing starts, etc.) as primary inputs, together with the Economic Forecast Council survey.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Data Sources: Statistics Canada (Labour Force Survey, CPI, retail sales, housing starts, GDP); ... Economic Forecast Council (13-member surveys for B.C./Canada/international GDP ...

dependencies.basis: The Annual Service Plan Report is the statutory accountability document for the BC Assessment Authority itself, reporting performance against the mandate to produce the uniform assessment roll.
dependencies.evidence_quote: BC Assessment is a provincial Crown corporation with the legislated mandate to establish and maintain property assessments that are uniform in the whole of British Columbia, in accordance with the Assessment Act. While BC Assessment has no direct role in property taxation, it plays an integral and impartial role in the provincial property taxation system by producing an accurate and uniform assessment roll each year for over two million properties in the province.

dependencies.basis: The annual financial report presents actual results against the approved budget figures for revenues (including property taxes) and expenses.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Consolidated revenues of $3.1 billion (2024 - $3.2 billion) ... Property and business Taxes: $142.8 million increase from property tax rate increases ...
